challenges.name: sbom-diff-quiz
challenges.title: Read the SBOM diff of release 2026.10.3
challenges.description: Two findings from the SBOM diff between releases 2026.10.2 and 2026.10.3 of the CodeDev API: a package whose hash changed while its version did not, and a version change that a diff tool reported as a downgrade.

questions.question:
The same component in the SBOMs of two releases:

release 2026.10.2 (sbom.cdx.json)
{ "name": "event-stream", "version": "3.3.6", "purl": "pkg:npm/event-stream@3.3.6",
  "hashes": [{ "alg": "SHA-512", "content": "8a2c71...e04b" }] }

release 2026.10.3 (sbom.cdx.json)
{ "name": "event-stream", "version": "3.3.6", "purl": "pkg:npm/event-stream@3.3.6",
  "hashes": [{ "alg": "SHA-512", "content": "f19d03...7a2e" }] }

package-lock.json diff for the same entry:
-  "resolved": "https://registry.npmjs.org/event-stream/-/event-stream-3.3.6.tgz",
+  "resolved": "https://npm-mirror.codedev.test/event-stream/-/event-stream-3.3.6.tgz",

Statement: "This finding needs investigation before the release ships: the public npm registry does not let a published version be replaced with different content, so a different tarball for 3.3.6 means a different source or a modified file."
questions.explanation: True. npm treats a published name@version as immutable: even after an unpublish, the same version number cannot be published again with new content. So the same version with a different hash cannot be a normal upgrade. The lockfile diff shows where to look: the tarball now comes from a mirror, and the mirror served different bytes. That can be a misconfigured mirror, a cache that was written to, or an attack; in every case the release should wait until someone compares the two tarballs. The misconception is that "same version" means "same code" and that a hash change without a version change is harmless noise from the SBOM generator.

questions.question:
Output of the team's first SBOM diff script and the CI policy that uses it:

$ node scripts/sbom-diff.mjs sbom-2026.10.2.json sbom-2026.10.3.json
version changed  pkg:npm/date-utils   1.9.0 -> 1.10.0   downgrade
version changed  pkg:npm/zod          3.23.8 -> 3.24.1  upgrade

// scripts/sbom-diff.mjs
const direction = to > from ? "upgrade" : "downgrade";

# ci policy
fail the release when any dependency is downgraded

Statement: "The release moved date-utils to an older version, so the CI policy is right to fail it."
questions.explanation: False. The script compares versions as strings, character by character: "1.1" is less than "1.9" because "1" sorts before "9", so "1.10.0" > "1.9.0" is false for strings. Under semantic versioning 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.0: compare major, minor and patch as numbers (1 = 1, then 10 > 9). The release upgraded date-utils, and the policy failed for a bug in the diff script. The misconception is that version strings can be compared like any other string; prerelease tags (1.0.0-rc.1 < 1.0.0) need the semver rules too.

challenges.name: sbom-diff
challenges.title: SBOM diff between two releases
challenges.description:
Before each CodeDev release, CI generates a CycloneDX SBOM of the API and compares it with the SBOM of the previous release. Reviewers read the diff, not the 1,800 components. Write `diffSboms(before, after)`.

**Input** (stdin, JSON): `{ "before": <SBOM>, "after": <SBOM> }`. An SBOM is a CycloneDX JSON subset: `{ "bomFormat": "CycloneDX", "specVersion": "1.6", "components": [...] }`. A component may have `type`, `name`, `group`, `version`, `purl`, `licenses` (items `{ "license": { "id": ... } }`, `{ "license": { "name": ... } }` or `{ "expression": ... }`), `hashes` (`[{ "alg": "SHA-256", "content": "<hex>" }]`) and nested `components` (any depth). `components` may be missing (no components). Ignore `metadata`.

**Rules**
1. Walk all components, nested ones included, in document order (a parent, then its children, then the next sibling).
2. **Key**: the purl without its version, qualifiers and subpath, with every `%40` (any case) replaced by `@`. The version is what follows the last `@` that comes after the last `/`, before `?` (qualifiers) and `#` (subpath): `pkg:npm/%40codedev/ui@2.1.0?vcs_url=x#dist` has the key `pkg:npm/@codedev/ui`. **No purl** (missing or empty): the key is `name:<group>/<name>`, or `name:<name>` when there is no group.
3. **Version**: the `version` field; when it is missing or empty, the version written in the purl (`""` if there is none).
4. **Duplicates**: within one SBOM, a key + version seen again is a duplicate: keep the first one and count it in `duplicatesCollapsed`. The same key with different versions (npm can install two versions of a package) are different entries.
5. **Licenses** of an entry: for each item, `license.id`, else `license.name`, else `expression`; unique and sorted. **Hashes**: by `alg` (exact string, first one wins), `content` compared in lowercase.
6. For each key, compare the versions present before and after:
   - a version present in both: report `licenseChanged` when the license lists differ, and `hashChanged` (suspicious: same version, different bytes) with the algorithms present on both sides whose content differs. Algorithms present on one side only are not compared.
   - the remaining versions: if exactly one is left before and exactly one after, it is a `versionChanged` `{ key, from, to, direction, sameMajor }` (also report `licenseChanged` with `version` = the new version when their licenses differ; never `hashChanged`). Otherwise every remaining old version is `removed` and every remaining new one is `added`.
7. **direction** follows SemVer 2.0.0 precedence: `upgrade`, `downgrade`, `same` (only build metadata differs) or `unknown` when either version is not `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-prerelease][+build]` (an optional leading `v` is allowed; no leading zeros in MAJOR, MINOR or PATCH). A version with a prerelease is lower than the same version without one; prerelease identifiers are compared left to right, numeric ones as numbers, others as strings, numeric lower than non-numeric, and a shorter list is lower when all shared identifiers are equal. **sameMajor**: true when both versions are valid semver with the same major, else false.

**Output** (one JSON object): `{ "added": [{ key, version }], "removed": [{ key, version }], "versionChanged": [{ key, from, to, direction, sameMajor }], "licenseChanged": [{ key, version, from: [...], to: [...] }], "hashChanged": [{ key, version, algs: [...] }], "summary": { before, after, added, removed, versionChanged, licenseChanged, hashChanged, duplicatesCollapsed, withoutPurl } }`. Sort every list by key, then version (`versionChanged` by key); compare strings by code unit (`<`), not `localeCompare`. `summary.before` and `summary.after` count the entries (key + version) after removing duplicates; `withoutPurl` counts the distinct `name:` keys over both SBOMs; the other counts are list lengths.

**Invalid input**: if `before` (checked first) or `after` is not an object with `bomFormat` `"CycloneDX"` and an array (or missing) `components`, print `{ "error": "before is not a CycloneDX SBOM" }` (or `after`). If a component, nested or not, has neither a purl nor a name, print `{ "error": "before has a component without purl or name" }` (or `after`).

Up to 2,000 components per SBOM. Standard library only.
hints: If you key components by the full purl, how does an upgrade from lodash 4.17.20 to 4.17.21 appear in your report: as one change, or as one package added and another removed? And what would a reviewer miss in that noise?

Check three places: where you cut the version out of the purl (after the last @ that follows the last /, before ? and #), whether your walk recurses into every components array, and how you compare versions: for strings, "1.10.0" < "1.9.0" is true.

A similar case on other input: pkg:pypi/requests@2.31.0?extension=whl has the key pkg:pypi/requests and the version 2.31.0. For 2.0.0-beta.11 against 2.0.0-beta.2, beta equals beta, then 11 and 2 are both numeric, so they compare as numbers and beta.11 is the newer one; 2.0.0 is newer than both because it has no prerelease.

tests.name: An upgrade, a new scoped package and a removed package
License change on a major upgrade, same-version hash change, incomparable hash algorithms
Nested components, %40 and @ in purls, qualifiers, subpath and a version only in the purl
Semver direction: 1.9.0 to 1.10.0, prereleases, build metadata, downgrades and non-semver
Duplicates, two versions of one package and components without purl
Large SBOMs: 160 nested components with scattered changes
Invalid input: the after document is SPDX, not CycloneDX

expected.error: after is not a CycloneDX SBOM

tests.name: Invalid input: a nested component without purl or name

expected.error: before has a component without purl or name
